claims.claim: Visa organises its value-added services (VAS) sold to partners into four portfolios: Issuing Solutions, Acceptance Solutions, Risk and Security Solutions, and Advisory and Other Services.

claims.label: Verified
claims.note: FY ended 2025-09-30; filed Nov 2025. 10-K sizes the four portfolios at ~$125B, $95B, $150B, $150B of a $520B annual revenue opportunity.

claims.claim: VAS revenue was $10.9B in fiscal 2025, up 24%, showing value-added services are a material line sold on top of core network processing.
claims.quote: For fiscal 2025, 2024, and 2023, revenue from value-added services was $10.9 billion, $8.8 billion and $7.2 billion, respectively.
claims.title: Visa Inc. Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended September 30, 2025
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Growth attributed to Issuing Solutions, Advisory and Other Services and Acceptance Solutions.

claims.claim: Visa describes its partner-facing offer as a four-layer 'Visa as a Service' stack (foundation, services, solutions, access) so capabilities can be sold unbundled to any client type.
claims.quote: our Visa as a Service stack, which has four layers: the foundation layer, the services layer, the solutions layer and the access layer.
claims.title: Visa Inc. Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended September 30, 2025
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Access layer is on-demand APIs, an MCP server for AI systems, and fully managed solutions.

claims.claim: Investor Day frames the unbundled catalogue as Acceptance-as-a-Service, Risk-as-a-Service, Wallet-as-a-Service and Cybersecurity-as-a-Service, distributed over the Visa Developer Platform.
claims.quote: Our unbundled capabilities create Visa-as-a-Service Visa Protect for A2A Risk-as-a-Service Select examples of unbundled services Acceptance-as-a-Service
claims.title: Visa 2025 Investor Day (consolidated presentation)
claims.label: Vendor
claims.note: Slide 106; quote is slide text as extracted. Predates Capital One/Discover close (2025-05-18); not relevant to Visa.

claims.claim: Visa's VAS go-to-market targets financial institutions, fintechs, big tech, acquirers, software vendors, PSPs and sellers through ~450 specialised salespeople and ~5,400 resale partners.
claims.quote: VAS Go-To-Market Engine Financial Institutions ~450 Specialized Salespeople ~5,400 Resale Partners Distribution Channels
claims.title: Visa 2025 Investor Day (consolidated presentation)
claims.label: Vendor
claims.note: Slide 90. Indicates VAS is sold both direct and via resale partners (processors, PSPs).

claims.claim: Issuer processing and core banking are sold as VAS, delivered mainly by Visa DPS (issuer processor) and Pismo (cloud core banking).
claims.quote: Our last two solutions are Issuer Processing and Core Banking, which are primarily delivered by our Visa DPS and Pismo platforms.
claims.title: Visa Inc. Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended September 30, 2025
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Sold direct to issuers; DPS Forward is the API-based modular variant.

claims.claim: Visa DPS bundles value-added issuer services beyond processing: fraud mitigation, dispute management, data analytics, campaign management, digital solutions and contact-centre services.
claims.quote: Visa DPS is a large issuer processor of multi-network transactions, which also provides a wide range of value-added services, including fraud mitigation, dispute management
claims.title: Visa Inc. Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended September 30, 2025
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Multi-network means DPS also drives non-Visa debit/ATM networks for issuers.

claims.claim: DPS Forward is Visa's API-based issuer-processing product for digital issuers and fintechs, exposed on the Visa Developer Center.
claims.quote: DPS Forward is a digital issuer processing service that provides you agility and operational excellence at scale.
claims.title: Visa Developer - DPS Forward
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Listed for Issuer Banks, Independent Developers, Issuer Banks for Small Business.

claims.claim: Visa DPS claims a quarter of VisaNet global debit authorizations and exposes its APIs through the Visa Developer Center.
claims.quote: Visa clients can access APIs directly in the Visa Developer Center.
claims.title: DPS Processing | Visa
claims.label: Vendor
claims.note: Page also shows '52 B annual authorizations', '$2.6 T payment volume', '25 % share of VisaNet global debit authorizations' (FY24 footnotes).

claims.claim: Smarter Stand-In Processing is an issuer VAS in which Visa's AI authorises on the issuer's behalf during outages.
claims.quote: our Smarter Stand-In Processing uses AI to authorize transactions on behalf of issuers in the event of system outages or maintenance
claims.title: Visa Inc. Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended September 30, 2025
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Investor Day slide 82 claims 1,500+ issuers implemented, ~30%+ authorization uplift.

claims.claim: Visa Token Service (VTS) is the network tokenisation service for issuers and token requestors; Visa reports more than 16 billion tokens provisioned.
claims.quote: As of September 30, 2025, Visa has provisioned more than 16 billion tokens.
claims.title: Visa Inc. Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended September 30, 2025
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Core network service. Developer page lists VTS for Issuer Banks, Merchants, Independent Developers.

claims.claim: Rules make an issuer that uses VTS responsible for cardholder identity validation, token provisioning decisions and credential updates.
claims.quote: An Issuer that uses the Visa Token Service (VTS) may participate in one or more Token Requestor solutions available through the applicable enrollment process.
claims.title: Visa Core Rules and Visa Product and Service Rules, 18 April 2026
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Rule ID# 0031128, section 4.1.15.1.

claims.claim: Visa Advanced Authorization (real-time risk score) and Visa Risk Manager (rules/case tool) are issuer fraud products; in Europe Visa auto-enrols all issuers, making them de facto mandatory there.
claims.quote: Visa will enroll all Issuers in the Visa Advanced Authorization service for all Card-Absent Environment Transactions, and the Visa Risk Manager service.
claims.title: Visa Core Rules and Visa Product and Service Rules, 18 April 2026
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Section 10.12.1.1. AP/LAC: issuers must implement a risk-scoring tool and/or VAA+VRM; named Gulf/MENA countries must accept the VAA score.

claims.claim: Visa Risk Manager is positioned as a network-agnostic issuer fraud-strategy console; Visa claims 8,000+ banks use VAA and VRM.
claims.quote: provides issuers with control and flexibility to manage their risk strategies and tolerance across all card payments
claims.title: Optimize authorization performance with Visa Protect | Visa
claims.label: Vendor
claims.note: Page also states '8K+ banks rely on VAA and VRM to identify fraud' and '400 risk attributes are analyzed'.

claims.claim: Visa Provisioning Intelligence (token-provisioning risk score) is auto-enrolled for all issuers in Europe with an opt-out only for low-fraud issuers.
claims.quote: In the Europe Region: Visa will enroll all Issuers in the Visa Provisioning Intelligence Service.
claims.title: Visa Core Rules and Visa Product and Service Rules, 18 April 2026
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Section 10.11.5.2; opt-out if token fraud-to-sales under 2.5 bps over 12 months.

claims.claim: Visa Account Updater is a mandatory issuer service in most regions: issuers must enrol their BINs, with listed exceptions (commercial, prepaid, ATM-only BINs).
claims.quote: An Issuer must enroll its BINs in Visa Account Updater (VAU), as follows:
claims.title: Visa Core Rules and Visa Product and Service Rules, 18 April 2026
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Section 8.6.1.1 'Visa Processing Services'. Merchants access VAU only through acquirers.

claims.claim: Issuers in CEMEA, Europe and LAC must participate in the Visa Alias Directory Service, the directory that resolves aliases for Visa Direct push payments.
claims.quote: Participate in the Visa Alias Directory Service (VADS) in line with adoption timeframes
claims.title: Visa Core Rules and Visa Product and Service Rules, 18 April 2026
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Section 7.3.12.1; references the Visa Direct for Card Processing Guide effective 18 April 2026.

claims.claim: Issuers wanting their cards to work at ATMs must certify for the Visa Global ATM Network; US consumer-card issuers must participate.
claims.quote: To participate in the Visa Global ATM Network, an Issuer must successfully complete certification with Visa.
claims.title: Visa Core Rules and Visa Product and Service Rules, 18 April 2026
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Section 6.2.1.1 adds: 'In the US Region: A Visa Consumer Card Issuer must participate in the Visa ATM Network.'

claims.claim: Issuers that do not run their own 3-D Secure access control server must use Visa Consumer Authentication Service or a registered ACS provider.
claims.quote: The Visa Consumer Authentication Service – An ACS service provider listed on the Visa Global Registry of Service Providers
claims.title: Visa Core Rules and Visa Product and Service Rules, 18 April 2026
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Section 10.15.2.2. VCAS is thus a value-added issuer service positioned against third-party ACS vendors.

claims.claim: Visa Flex Credential is an issuing product letting one credential switch among funding sources; Visa reports 20+ signed clients in 20+ countries.
claims.quote: Visa Flex Credential allows consumers to use a single Visa payment credential to access and switch between multiple funding sources, like debit and credit.
claims.title: Visa Inc. Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended September 30, 2025
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Developer catalogue lists 'Visa Flex Credential' for acquirers, issuers and merchants.

claims.claim: Visa sells issuers a loyalty/benefits layer including a Merchant Offers Program of Visa-negotiated offers, and lists Visa Online as the enrolment portal for community issuers.
claims.quote: Includes over 30 offers, negotiated and managed by Visa, and is a cost-effective way to deliver value to your cardholders.
claims.title: Visa Community Issuer Resources | Visa
claims.label: Vendor
claims.note: Page calls Visa Online 'Your one-stop shop destination for doing business with Visa.' Developer catalogue separately lists Visa Offers Platform, Visa Offers Network, Visa Merchant Offers Resource Center, Visa Digital Benefits Platform.

claims.claim: The Rules distinguish mandatory core services from optional services for commercial card products (Table 4-22), e.g. some assistance services are optional for Visa Corporate Prepaid Cards.
claims.quote: This is an optional service for Visa Corporate Prepaid Cards.
claims.title: Visa Core Rules and Visa Product and Service Rules, 18 April 2026
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Footnote to 'Table 4-22: Visa Commercial Card Mandatory Core Services'. Public rules do not contain one consolidated mandatory/optional services list.

claims.claim: VisaNet Connect - Issuing gives issuers and their processors a direct VisaNet interface as a developer product.
claims.quote: Direct access to VisaNet to securely enable innovative payments solutions
claims.title: Browse Products | Visa Developer Center
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Catalogue also lists VisaNet Connect - Acceptance for the acquiring side.

claims.claim: Visa Acceptance Solutions is sold to acquirers and sellers as modular VAS layered on a gateway function (formerly CyberSource).

claims.label: Verified

claims.claim: The Visa Acceptance Platform is sold to acquirers, PSPs, ISVs and sellers; Cybersource and Authorize.net are the named platform brands.

claims.label: Verified

claims.label: Vendor

claims.title: Visa Inc. Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended September 30, 2025

claims.title: Visa Inc. Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended September 30, 2025

claims.label: Verified

claims.label: Verified

claims.title: Visa Inc. Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended September 30, 2025

claims.claim: VisaNet Connect - Acceptance offers acquirers/merchants a direct interface to VisaNet for in-store, in-app and online payments.

claims.label: Verified

claims.note: Section 7.2.1.1 'Access to Visa Systems'.

claims.title: Visa · GitHub
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: 10-K: 'Visa Intelligent Commerce is an innovative offering in this space that integrates Visa's tokenization technology with authentication and predictive analytics'. Also 'trusted-agent-protocol' repo.
